findings.label: FOLLOW-ON
findings.text: The two new outcome assertions compare the stored status against STATUS_ABORTED imported from the module under test (tests/test_request_receipts.py:754 and :787), so moving the constant's value moves both sides of the assertion -- the same shape the repair removed for the self-answered sentinel one line below at :755, which now names the literal "(router)". Input that demonstrates it: STATUS_ABORTED in imas_ambix/agent/request_receipts.py:66 changed to "caller-left" leaves the status half of every row assertion following the constant, while the upstream half at :755 and :788 still fails on its literal; I did not run that mutation inside this node's 45-minute fence, so this is reasoned from the two assertion forms in the same test rather than demonstrated, and it is reported as a FOLLOW-ON rather than a blocking defect because the value that a reader sums traffic around is the upstream sentinel, which the repair did pin. The stronger fix is the one already applied to the sentinel: assert the string in one place and let the module's constant track it. Severity low: the row's status strings are the record's own vocabulary and the module defines them in the docstring beside their meanings, so a move is visible in review even when the test agrees with it.

findings.label: FOLLOW-ON
findings.text: The self-answered departure is sampled one event-loop turn after the status line is sent and before the body is sent, so a caller that goes away inside that window is still recorded completed, which is the outcome the router intended rather than the one the caller received. Concrete input: a client that sends GET /v1/models and aborts its transport in the microseconds between the router's http.response.start and its http.response.body leaves a completed row. The window is real but small on the wire and it is the relay's own design too -- the relay reads the disconnect only while its body loop is running -- and the docstring states why the watch must not outlive the send. A mutation cannot demonstrate it without a timing harness that controls the transport between two sends, which is why it is a FOLLOW-ON observation and not a Finding.

justifications.durability: Every scenario in the node's checklist was driven at the reviewed head through a live uvicorn router on 127.0.0.1 with a real aiohttp engine and read from the receipts JSONL on disk (logs/drive-srun.log): a completed relay wrote one completed row; an engine refusing 503 wrote one failed row; an engine aborting its transport mid-body wrote one failed row; a caller dropping mid-relay wrote one aborted row; a caller dropping mid-upload wrote one aborted row with upstream (router) and model ""; an unrouted path's 404 wrote one failed row; a catalog GET whose caller read it wrote one completed row; and a catalog GET whose caller had already gone wrote one aborted row. The mid-upload row is the repair under review and the same instrument at the pre-repair head recorded rows=0 for it (the earlier review's logs/drive.log line 14), so the instrument is shown to distinguish the two revisions rather than agreeing with each. The sampling ceiling still bounds volume: at inf, 40 offered requests wrote 40 rows all with fraction 1.0; at 2 per second, 40 offered wrote 10 rows whose fractions run from 0.0606 to 1.0. Eleven fewer than a perfect ten-row rate at the reviewed head's 800/s observed rate is the expected droop of a sliding window, not a defect. What keeps it from full marks is that a departure arriving after the self-answered watch samples but before its body is written still records what the router intended rather than what the caller received, which the second FOLLOW-ON states.
justifications.evidence: All of the above was re-derived at the reviewed head and read from the stored rows, not from the module's behaviour in the abstract or from the run's manifest. One of the four declared negative controls was replayed verbatim inside the fence: the mutation named on the first line of logs/negative-control-sentinel-moved-to-an-engine-origin.log, applied to the checked-out request_receipts.py, reddened tests/test_request_receipts.py with 4 failed, 14 passed -- the same count the reviewed run's own log records for it -- and the two row assertions that carry the literal both failed, which is the pin the earlier review found missing. The module was then restored from HEAD and verified by sha256 (6a743d59173622f9f6627af15a99ccd8966e8364eeab9e6b79163130465383e4) with a clean git status. The checklist's fourth item is answered by inspection of every use of SELF_ANSWERED_UPSTREAM: it appears in tests only at the import and at the single equality assertion at :687, with both row assertions naming the literal, so no expectation for a reader-summed field is still computed from the module under test; the two status assertions that remain symbol-based are reported as the first FOLLOW-ON. The remaining three controls were not replayed before the fence expired, so their claims are asserted rather than re-derived; the manifest says so.
justifications.fit: The repair follows the file's own habits rather than importing new ones: the refusal funnel keeps its single exit and threads the new parameter through the existing signature shape; the mid-upload branch records through the same _record_self_answer helper the other self-answered paths use, with the same keyword-only http_status/caller_gone form the module's other optional parameters use; the departure is read on the same channel and with the same helper the relay already uses; and the outcome vocabulary is extended in the docstring where the labels are defined, with the reason for the caller_gone rule written beside the field rather than in a second place. The tests extend the repository's existing router harness (_body, _card, _invoke and the SSE engine from tests/test_agent_router) instead of building a parallel one, which is what the section's write path asks for.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The section's done-when is that every completed request appears once and that a failed or aborted request is recorded as such rather than dropped. At the reviewed head all seven outcomes the checklist names produce exactly one row, and the one path whose answer the caller never received is recorded as aborted rather than as the completed answer the router composed. The three gaps the earlier review recorded are closed on the evidence: the mid-upload departure leaves a row instead of none, the self-answered sites derive their status from what the caller received, and the sentinel is held by a literal with a single equality assertion pinning the constant. What remains between this and full marks is the sampling window in the second FOLLOW-ON rather than any path that records nothing or records an empty answer as a completed one: no driven path was found that records something the caller did not receive, and none that records nothing.
justifications.scope_discipline: The repair commit touches exactly the three paths the section names -- imas_ambix/agent/router.py, imas_ambix/agent/request_receipts.py and tests/test_request_receipts.py -- and nothing else in the diff. A scan of the added lines for plan labels, ticket references, version suffixes, changelog prose and author attribution returns no hits, and the commit message describes the mechanisms rather than citing the review that found them. The one thing the change deliberately did not do is collapse a caller that leaves mid-upload into failed, and that reasoning is sound on the evidence: the record now separates a caller that received an empty answer (failed, the refusal delivered) from a caller that received nothing (aborted), which the stored rows show at the reviewed head as the two distinct strings.
